answer: Sybil resistance via a decaying social-graph web-of-trust: each new agent must be vouched by at least k already-trusted peers whose edge weights form an anchor rooted in long-lived identities. Vouch edges expire on a yarrow schedule—half-life measured in epochs—so stale endorsements wither before a coordinated gale of sockpuppets can flood the graph. Admission weight is the product of path scores from the root set; agents below a threshold cannot mine or grade. Continuous re-anchoring of the root set by mutual continuous work prevents clique capture.
